topic: Why a larger light makes a softer shadow edge
audience: Adults photographing objects with a desk lamp
prior: Know that an opaque object blocks direct light; may think brightness controls edge width.
objective: Predict how changing the apparent size of a light changes the shadow edge when the object and screen stay fixed.
takeaway: The edge is softer where the object blocks only part of the light source.
tone: Conversational and curious; avoid camera jargon.

intro.description: Ask why the same toy casts shadows with different edge widths.
intro.must_show: Two views of the same toy and screen; a small light and a visibly wider light.

lesson.description: Hold the geometry fixed apart from the luminous area.
lesson.must_show: Lights have the same center and are equally far from the toy; toy and screen do not move.

mechanism.description: Trace rays from opposite edges of the wider source.
mechanism.must_show: A screen location blocked from one edge of the lamp can still receive light from the other edge.

result.description: Connect the wider region of partial blockage to the softer edge.
result.must_show: Side-by-side shadow edge transitions aligned to the same screen coordinates.

transfer.question: What happens if you cover the edges of the wider lamp and leave just its center lit?
transfer.answer: The shadow edge becomes sharper, all else equal.
transfer.reasoning: A smaller apparent source narrows the region where only part of the light can reach the screen.

facts.claim: Idealized straight-light-ray demonstration with a fixed opaque toy and screen, no extra light and no scattering.

constraints: Do not confuse the apparent size of the source with its brightness.
